name: code-implementation
description: Implement a change with a baseline captured first, per-file work pipelined, and a real verification gate before anything is staged for review.

task.help: What to implement. Specific beats broad — this template plans from what you write.

verify_command.help: The command that decides whether the change is done. The gate runs it and does not take the model's word for it.

baseline_command.help: Run BEFORE any edit, so a failure afterwards can be told apart from one that was already there.

steering_examples.description: Add a --dry-run flag to the snapshot command. Verify with: make lint && pytest tests/test_snapshot.py
The plan missed the CLI help text — splice a file into the foreach for docs/cli.md before the verify gate.

metadata.when_not_to_use: not for deciding WHAT to build — use project-planning first

config.prompt:
Plan this change.

List the files to touch and what changes in each. Read enough of the code first that the plan reflects what is there rather than what would be convenient — a plan that names a function which does not exist costs more than no plan.

Return the file list explicitly; the next step fans out over it.

Task:
{{inputs.task}}

Baseline (what was already failing before any edit):
{{nodes.baseline.output}}

Extract just the file list from the plan below, in the order they should be worked.

Return JSON: {"files": [{"path": "…", "change": "one line"}]}.

Plan:
{{nodes.plan.output}}
Verification is still failing after its retries. Approve to accept the change as-is, or deny to stop here.

Compare the baseline against the final verification. Classify each difference as: regression (this change broke it), pre-existing (it was already failing), or resolved (this change fixed it).

The distinction is the point — a pre-existing failure blamed on this change sends someone to debug the wrong commit.

Return JSON: {"regressions": ["…"], "pre_existing": ["…"], "resolved": ["…"]}.

Baseline:
{{nodes.baseline.output}}

Final:
{{nodes.verify.output}}
